list: List of cards by index number in Pokémon Trading Card Game 2

7.name: Double Colorless Energy
7.text: Provides ColorlessColorless energy. Doesn't count as a basic Energy card.

8.name: Potion Energy
8.text: If you play this card from your hand, remove 1 damage counter from the Pokemon you attach it to, if it has any. Potion Energy provides Colorless Energy. (Doesn't count as a basic Energy card.)

9.name: Full Heal Energy
9.text: If you play this card from your hand, the Pokemon you attach it to is no longer Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned. Full Heal Energy provides Colorless Energy. (Doesn't count as a basic Energy card.)

11.name: Recycle Energy
11.text: Recycle Energy provides Colorless Energy. (Doesn't count as a basic Energy card.) If this card is put into your discard pile from play, return it to your hand.

12.name: Bulbasaur
12.flavor: It can go for days without eating a single morsel. In the bulb on its back, it stores energy.

13.name: Bulbasaur

attacks.name: Leech Seed
attacks.text: Unless all damage from this attack is prevented, you may remove 1 damage counter from Bulbasaur.

13.flavor: There is a plant seed on its back right from the day this Pokemon is born. The seed slowly grows larger.

14.name: Bulbasaur

attacks.name: First Aid
attacks.text: Remove 1 damage counter from Bulbasaur.

attacks.name: Poison Seed
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

14.flavor: A strange seed was planted on its back at birth. The plant sprouts and grows with this Pokemon.

15.name: Ivysaur

attacks.name: Poisonpowder
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

15.flavor: There is a plant bulb on its back. When it absorbs nutrients, the bulb is said to blossom into a large flower.

16.name: Ivysaur

attacks.name: Leech Seed
attacks.text: Unless all damage from this attack is prevented, you may remove one damage counter from Ivysaur.

16.flavor: The bulb on its back grows by drawing energy. It gives off an aroma when it is ready to bloom.

17.name: Dark Ivysaur

attacks.name: Vine Pull
attacks.text: Once during your turn when Dark Ivysaur retreats, if your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and switches it with the Defending Pokemon.

attacks.name: Fury Strikes
attacks.text: Your opponent puts 3 markers onto his or her Pokemon (divided as he or she chooses). (More than 1 marker can be put on the same Pokemon.) Then, this attack does 10 damage to each Pokemon for each marker on it. Don't apply Weakness and Resistance. Remove the markers at the end of the turn.

17.flavor: It uses well-developed vines, which extend from its back, to freely manipulate and pull opponents without looking.

18.name: Venusaur

attacks.name: Solar Power
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may use this power. Your Active Pokemon and the Defending Pokemon are no longer Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned. This power can't be used if Venusaur is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Mega Drain
attacks.text: Remove a number of damage counters from Venusaur equal to half the damage done to the Defending Pokemon (after applying Weakness and Resistance) (rounded up to the nearest 10). If Venusaur has fewer damage counters than that, remove all of them.

18.flavor: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.

19.name: Venusaur

attacks.name: Energy Trans
attacks.text: As often as you like during your turn (before your attack), you may take 1 Grass Energy card attached to 1 of your Pokemon and attach it to a different one. This power can't be used if Venusaur is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

19.flavor: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.

20.name: Venusaur

attacks.name: Energy Trans
attacks.text: As often as you like during your turn (before your attack), you may take 1 Grass Energy card attached to 1 of your Pokemon and attach it to a different one. This power can't be used if Venusaur is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

20.flavor: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.

21.name: Dark Venusaur

attacks.name: Horrid Pollen
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. If 1 is heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep and Poisoned. If both are heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused and Poisoned. If both are tails, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed and Poisoned.

21.flavor: When its large flower opens, there is a million-to-one chance that the pollen it spreads will inflict a status ailment on the opponent.
21.from: Unnumbered Promotional and Best of Game prints

22.name: Caterpie

attacks.name: String Shot
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

22.flavor: It is covered with a green skin. When it grows, it sheds the skin, covers itself with silk, and becomes a cocoon.

23.name: Metapod

attacks.name: Green Shield
attacks.text: As long as Metapod is in play, ignore Weakness when any of your Grass Pokemon are damaged. This power stops working while Metapod is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Mysterious Powder
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

23.flavor: If it receives strong shock before its shell hardens, the inside pops out, so beware.

24.name: Metapod

attacks.name: Stiffen
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, prevent all damage done to Metapod during your opponent's next turn. (Any other effects of attacks still happen.)

attacks.name: Stun Spore
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

24.flavor: Even though it is encased in a sturdy shell, the body inside is tender. It can't withstand a harsh attack.

25.name: Butterfree

attacks.name: Whirlwind
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and switches it with the Defending Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

attacks.name: Mega Drain
attacks.text: Remove a number of damage counters from Butterfree equal to half the damage done to the Defending Pokemon (after applying Weakness and Resistance) (rounded up to the nearest 10).

25.flavor: The wings are protected by a rain-repellent dust. As a result, this Pokemon can fly about even in rain.

26.name: Weedle

attacks.name: Poison Sting
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

26.flavor: Often found in forests and grasslands. It has a sharp, toxic barb of around 5 cm on top of its head.

27.name: Weedle

attacks.name: Poison Horn
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

27.flavor: Often found in forests, eating leaves. It has a sharp, venomous stinger on its head.

28.name: Kakuna

attacks.name: Stiffen
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, prevent all damage done to Kakuna during your opponent's next turn. (Any other effects of attacks still happen.)

attacks.name: Poisonpowder
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

28.flavor: This Pokemon is in a temporary stage while making its body. It is almost completely unable to move on its own.

29.name: Kakuna

attacks.name: Poison Fluid
attacks.text: If Kakuna is damaged by an opponent's attack (even if Kakuna is Knocked Out), the Attacking Pokemon is now Poisoned. This power stops working while Kakuna is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

29.flavor: Almost incapable of moving, this Pokemon can only harden its shell to protect itself from predators.

30.name: Beedrill

attacks.name: Twineedle
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads.

attacks.name: Poison Sting
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

30.flavor: May appear in a swarm. Flies at violent speeds, all the while stabbing with the toxic stinger on its rear.

31.name: Ekans

attacks.name: Spit Poison
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Wrap
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

31.flavor: Inhabits cemeteries. It flicks its tongue in and out to sense danger in its surroundings.

32.name: Ekans

attacks.name: Poison Sting
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

32.flavor: A carnivore that swallows its prey whole. Pidgeys and Spearows are its favorite food.

33.name: Arbok

attacks.name: Terror Strike
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads and if your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and switches it with the Defending Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

attacks.name: Poison Fang
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

33.flavor: The pattern on its belly appears to be a frightening face. Weak foes will flee just at the sight of the pattern.

34.name: Arbok

attacks.name: Wrap
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Deadly Poison
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned. If the Defending Pokemon was already Poisoned, this attack does 10 more damage.

34.flavor: It is rumored that the ferocious warning markings on its belly differ from area to area.

35.name: Dark Arbok

attacks.name: Stare
attacks.text: Choose 1 of your opponent's Pokemon. This attack does 10 damage to that Pokemon. Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for this attack. (Any other effects that would happen after applying Weakness and Resistance still happen.) If that Pokemon has a Pokemon Power, that power stops working until the end of your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Poison Vapor
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned. This attack does 10 damage to each of your opponent's Benched Pokemon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

35.flavor: Freezes its prey with its stare. If you should encounter one, remember not to look into its eyes.

36.name: Nidoran F

attacks.name: Tail Whip
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon can't attack Nidoran  F during your opponent's next turn. (Benching either Pokemon ends this effect.)

attacks.name: Poison Sting
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

36.flavor: Although small, its venomous barbs render this Pokemon dangerous. The female has smaller horns.

37.name: Nidoran F

attacks.name: Fury Swipes
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 10 damage times the number of heads.

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokemon named Nidoran M or Nidoran F and put it onto your Bench. Shuffle your deck afterward. (You can't use this attack if your Bench is full.)

37.flavor: Though small, it must be treated with caution because of its powerfully toxic barbs. The female has smaller horns.

38.name: Nidorina

attacks.name: Strength in Numbers
attacks.text: Does 10 more damage for each of your Benched Nidoran M, Nidoran F, Nidorino, Nidorina, Nidoking, and Nidoqueen.

attacks.name: Fury Swipes
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads.

38.flavor: The female's horn develops slowly. Prefers physical attacks such as clawing and biting.

39.name: Nidorina

attacks.name: Supersonic
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Double Kick
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads.

39.flavor: The female has a gentle temperament. It emits ultrasonic cries that have the power to befuddle foes.

40.name: Nidoqueen

attacks.name: Boyfriends
attacks.text: Does 20 damage plus 20 more damage for each Nidoking you have in play.

40.flavor: The body is covered by stiff, needle-like scales. If it becomes excited, the needles bristle outwards.

41.name: Nidoran M

attacks.name: Horn Hazard
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

41.flavor: Its large ears are flapped like wings when it is listening to distant sounds. It extends toxic barbs when angered.

42.name: Nidoran M

attacks.name: Focus Energy
attacks.text: During your next turn, Nidoran M's Horn Rush attack's base damage is doubled.

attacks.name: Horn Rush
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

42.flavor: Stiffens its ears to sense danger. The larger its horns, the more powerful its secreted venom.

43.name: Nidorino

attacks.name: Swift Lunge
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing and this Pokemon does 20 damage to itself.

43.flavor: An aggressive Pokemon that is quick to attack. The horn on its head secretes a powerful venom.

44.name: Nidorino

attacks.name: Double Kick
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads.

44.flavor: It is easily angered. By swinging its well-developed horn wildly, it can even punch through diamond.

45.name: Nidoking

attacks.name: Thrash
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 damage plus 10 more damage; if tails, this attack does 30 damage and Nidoking does 10 damage to itself.

attacks.name: Toxic
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned. It now takes 20 Poison damage instead of 10 after each player's turn (even if it was already Poisoned).

45.flavor: It is recognized by its rock-hard hide and its extended horn. Be careful with the horn as it contains venom.

46.name: Zubat
46.flavor: Lives in dark caves. Can occasionally be seen at night, when it flies in search of food.

47.name: Zubat

attacks.name: Supersonic
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Leech Life
attacks.text: Remove a number of damage counters from Zubat equal to the damage done to the Defending Pokemon (after applying Weakness and Resistance). If Zubat has fewer damage counters than that, remove all of them.

47.flavor: It has no eyes. Instead, it relies on its ultrasonic cries for echo location to flit about in darkness.

48.name: Zubat

attacks.name: Suspicious Soundwave
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

48.flavor: Forms colonies in perpetually dark places. Uses ultrasonic waves to identify and approach targets.

49.name: Golbat

attacks.name: Leech Life
attacks.text: Heal from this Pokemon the same amount of damage you did to the Defending Pokemon.

attacks.name: Nosedive
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this Pokemon does 40 damage to itself.

49.flavor: Once it strikes, it will not stop draining energy from the victim even if it gets too heavy to fly.

50.name: Golbat

attacks.name: Leech Life
attacks.text: Remove a number of damage counters from Golbat equal to the damage done to the Defending Pokemon (after applying Weakness and Resistance). If Golbat has fewer damage counters than that, remove all of them.

50.flavor: It clamps down on its prey with needle-sharp fangs and drains over 300cc of blood in one gulp.

51.name: Dark Golbat

attacks.name: Sneak Attack
attacks.text: Once during your turn, when you play this Pokemon from your hand, you may do 10 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokemon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

attacks.name: Flitter
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokemon. This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance.

51.flavor: Sneaks up silently on its prey and attacks it from behind, sometimes killing it with one bite.

52.name: Oddish

attacks.name: Stun Spore
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Sprout
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokemon named Oddish and put it onto your Bench. Shuffle your deck afterward. (You can't use this attack if your Bench is full.)

52.flavor: Its alias is Arukimendesu. At night, it is said to walk nearly 300 meters on its two roots.

53.name: Oddish

attacks.name: Sleep Powder
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Poisonpowder
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

53.flavor: It wanders around at night sowing its seeds to create more Oddishes.

54.name: Gloom

attacks.name: Poisonpowder
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Foul Odor
attacks.text: Both the Defending Pokemon and Gloom are now Confused (after doing damage).

54.flavor: Its pistils exude an incredibly foul odor. The horrid stench can cause fainting at a distance of 2 kilometers.

55.name: Dark Gloom

attacks.name: Pollen Stench
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused; if tails, your Active Pokemon is now Confused. This power can't be used if Dark Gloom is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Poisonpowder
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

55.flavor: Its pollen has such a strong smell that it even confuses itself at times.

56.name: Vileplume

attacks.name: Heal
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may flip a coin. If heads, remove 1 damage counter from 1 of your Pokemon. This power can't be used if Vileplume is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Petal Dance
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 40 damage times the number of heads. Vileplume is now Confused (after doing damage).

56.flavor: Its petals are the largest in the world. It fiendishly scatters allergy-causing pollen from its petals.

57.name: Dark Vileplume

attacks.name: Hay Fever
attacks.text: No Trainer cards can be played. This power stops working while Dark Vileplume is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Petal Whirlwind
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads. If you get 2 or more heads, Dark Vileplume is now Confused (after doing damage).

57.flavor: Perhaps because of their strong-smelling pollen, other Pokemon do not approach areas where Vileplumes live.

58.name: Paras

attacks.name: Spore
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

58.flavor: Growing out of the bug's back are mushrooms called tochukaso. The mushrooms grow with the bug host.

59.name: Paras

attacks.name: Scatter Spores
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokemon named Paras and put it onto your Bench. Shuffle your deck afterward. (You can't use this attack if your Bench is full.)

59.flavor: Burrows to suck tree roots. The mushrooms on its back grow by drawing nutrients from the bug host.

60.name: Parasect

attacks.name: Spore
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

60.flavor: It scatters toxic spores from the mushroom cap. In China, the spores are used as herbal medicine.

61.name: Parasect

attacks.name: Toxic Spore
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Leech Life
attacks.text: Heal from this Pokemon the same amount of damage you did to the Defending Pokemon.

61.flavor: A host-parasite pair in which the parasite mushroom has taken over the host bug. Prefers damp places.

62.name: Venonat

attacks.name: Stun Spore
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Leech Life
attacks.text: Remove a number of damage counters from Venonat equal to the damage done to the Defending Pokemon (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

62.flavor: Its eyes act as radar, enabling it to be active in darkness. The eyes can also shoot powerful beams.

63.name: Venonat

attacks.name: Disable
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, choose 1 of the Defending Pokemon's attacks. That Pokemon can't use that attack during your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Psybeam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

63.flavor: Lives in the shadows of tall trees where it eats bugs. It is attracted by light at night.

64.name: Venomoth

attacks.name: Stir Up Twister
attacks.text: Your opponent switches the Defending Pokemon with 1 of his or her Benched Pokemon. Then, switch your Active Pokemon with 1 of your Benched Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

attacks.name: Rainbow Powder
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed. If tails, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

64.flavor: The dustlike scales covering its wings are color-coded to indicate the kinds of poison it has.

65.name: Venomoth

attacks.name: Shift
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may change the type of Venomoth to the type of any other Pokemon in play other than Colorless. This power can't be used if Venomoth is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Venom Powder
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused and Poisoned.

65.flavor: The wings are covered with dustlike scales. Every time it flaps its wings, it looses highly toxic dust.

66.name: Bellsprout

attacks.name: Sway
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, prevent all damage done to this Pokemon during your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Stun Spore
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

66.flavor: A carnivorous Pokemon that traps and eats bugs. It appears to use its root feet to replenish moisture.

67.name: Bellsprout

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokemon named Bellsprout and put it onto your Bench. Shuffle your deck afterward. (You can't use this attack if your Bench is full.)

67.flavor: Its bud looks like a human face. Because of the bud, it is rumored to be a type of legendary mandrake plant.

68.name: Weepinbell

attacks.name: Regeneration
attacks.text: Remove all damage counters from this Pokemon. Discard all Evolution cards and Energy cards attached to this Pokemon.

attacks.name: Dissolve
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard 1 Energy card attached to the Defending Pokemon.

68.flavor: It spits out PoisonPowder to immobilize the enemy and then finishes it with a spray of Acid.

69.name: Weepinbell

attacks.name: Poisonpowder
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

69.flavor: The leafy parts act as cutters for slashing foes. It spits a fluid that dissolves everything.

70.name: Victreebel

attacks.name: Lure
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, choose 1 of them and switch it with his or her Active Pokemon.

attacks.name: Acid
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon can't retreat during your opponent's next turn.

70.flavor: Lures prey into its mouth with a honey-like aroma. The helpless prey is melted with a dissolving fluid.

71.name: Grimer

attacks.name: Poison Gas
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Sticky Hands
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 10 damage plus 20 more damage and the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed; if tails, this attack does 10 damage.

71.flavor: It has recently been found that Grimers are formed in waste-processing plants, and can move into towns via the sewers.

72.name: Grimer

attacks.name: Nasty Goo
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Minimize
attacks.text: All damage done by attacks to Grimer during your opponent's next turn is reduced by 20 (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

72.flavor: Sludge exposed to X rays from the moon transformed into Grimer. It loves feeding on filthy things.

73.name: Muk

attacks.name: Toxic Gas
attacks.text: Ignore all Pokemon Powers other than Toxic Gases. This power stops working while Muk is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Sludge
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

73.flavor: It is usually undetectable because it blends in with the ground. Touching it can cause deadly poisoning.

74.name: Dark Muk

attacks.name: Sticky Goo
attacks.text: As long as Dark Muk is your Active Pokemon, your opponent pays more to retreat his or her Active Pokemon. This power stops working while Dark Muk is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Sludge Punch
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

74.flavor: Muks appear suddenly, spreading sludge everywhere. Whenever one appears in a city, panic ensues.

75.name: Exeggcute

attacks.name: Hypnosis
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Leech Seed
attacks.text: Unless all damage from this attack is prevented, you may remove 1 damage counter from Exeggcute.

75.flavor: Even though it appears to be eggs of some sort, it was discovered to be a life-form more like plant seeds.

76.name: Exeggutor

attacks.name: Teleport
attacks.text: Switch Exeggutor with 1 of your Benched Pokemon.

attacks.name: Big Eggsplosion
attacks.text: Flip a number of coins equal to the number of Energy attached to Exeggutor. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

76.flavor: It is called The Walking Tropical Rainforest. Each of the nuts has a face and will of its own.

77.name: Koffing

attacks.name: Poison Gas
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

77.flavor: First discovered in a weapons factory, this Pokemon can now be found almost anywhere.

78.name: Koffing

attacks.name: Foul Gas
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned; if tails, it is now Confused.

78.flavor: Its thin, balloon-like body is inflated by horribly toxic gases. It reeks when it is nearby.

79.name: Koffing

attacks.name: Poison Gas
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Confusion Gas
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

79.flavor: In hot places, its internal gases could expand and explode without any warning. Be very careful!

80.name: Weezing

attacks.name: Poison Mist
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may flip a coin. If heads, until the end of your next turn, all Poisoned Pokemon take 20 damage instead of 10 damage from Poison after each player's turn. This power can't be used and stops working while this Pokemon is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Gas Explosion
attacks.text: This Pokemon does 30 damage to itself. If this attack Knocks Out the Defending Pokemon and your opponent chooses a new Active Pokemon, your opponent's new Active Pokemon becomes Poisoned.

80.flavor: Where two kinds of poison gases meet, two Koffings can fuse into a Weezing over many years.

81.name: Weezing

attacks.name: Smog
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Selfdestruct
attacks.text: Does 10 damage to each Pokemon on each player's Bench. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.) Weezing does 60 damage to itself.

81.flavor: Very rarely, a sudden mutation can result in two small Koffing twins becoming conjoined as a Weezing.

82.name: Dark Weezing

attacks.name: Mass Explosion
attacks.text: Does 20 damage times the total number of Koffings, Weezings, and Dark Weezings in play (Apply Weakness and Resistance.). Then, this attack does 20 damage to each Koffing, Weezing, and Dark Weezing (even your own). Don't apply Weakness and Resistance.

attacks.name: Stun Gas
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned; if tails, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

82.flavor: Researchers have observed these Pokemon reproducing in industrial waste sites.

83.name: Tangela

attacks.name: Bind
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Poisonpowder
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

83.flavor: Blue plant vines cloak the Pokemon's identity in a tangled mass. It entangles anything that gets close.

84.name: Tangela

attacks.name: Stun Spore
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Poison Whip
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Flamethrower
attacks.text: Discard 1 Fire Energy card attached to Charmeleon in order to use this attack.

97.name: Vulpix

attacks.name: Confuse Ray

97.flavor: While young, it has six gorgeous tails. When it grows, several new tails are sprouted.

98.flavor: At the time of birth, it has just one tail. The tail splits from its tip as it grows older.

attacks.name: Dancing Embers

attacks.name: Perplex

101.flavor: Occasionally bewitches trainers with its mysterious alluring powers.

102.flavor: A Pokemon with a friendly nature. However, it will bark fiercely at anything invading its territory.

103.flavor: Very protective of its territory. It will bark and bite to repel intruders from its space.

104.name: Growlithe
104.flavor: Very friendly and faithful to people. It will try to repel enemies by barking and biting.

105.flavor: A legendary Pokemon famous for its beauty. It looks almost as if it flies when it runs.

attacks.text: Discard 1 Fire Energy card attached to Arcanine in order to use this attack.

107.flavor: A Pokemon that is described in Chinese legends. It is said to race at an unbelievable speed.

attacks.name: Fireworks
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, discard 1 Energy card attached to this Pokemon.

108.flavor: Its hooves are 10 times harder than diamonds. It can trample anything completely flat in little time.

109.name: Ponyta

110.name: Ponyta

attacks.name: Ember
attacks.text: Discard 1 Fire Energy card attached to Ponyta in order to use this attack.

110.flavor: A gentle grass-eater, it will allow riders on its back. However, anyone attempting to do so must be careful to not get burned.

113.flavor: A wild, uncontrollable Pokemon. When running, it looks like a comet streaking through the sky.

117.flavor: Found at the mouths of volcanoes and extremely hard to spot. There are very few instances of capturing this Pokemon.

attacks.name: Flamethrower
attacks.text: Discard 1 Fire Energy card attached to Flareon in order to use this attack.

123.flavor: Known as the legendary bird of fire. Every flap of its wings creates a giant dazzle of flashing flames.

145.flavor: Its eyes are as transparent as crystals. From them, it shoots mysterious beams of light.

244.flavor: Its muscular body is so powerful, it must wear a power-save belt to be able to regulate its motions.

245.name: Machoke

attacks.name: Steady Punch
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

245.flavor: Its muscular body is so powerful, it must wear a power-save belt to be able to regulate its motions.

246.name: Machoke

attacks.name: Karate Chop
attacks.text: Does 50 damage minus 10 damage for each damage counter on Machoke.

attacks.name: Submission
attacks.text: Machoke does 20 damage to itself.

246.flavor: Its formidable body never gets tired. It helps people by doing work such as the moving of heavy goods.

247.name: Dark Machoke

attacks.name: Drag Off
attacks.text: Before doing damage, choose 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon and switch it with the Defending Pokemon. Do the damage to the new Defending Pokemon. This attack can't be used if your opponent has no Benched Pokemon.

attacks.name: Knock Back
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and switches it with the Defending Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

247.flavor: While normally peaceful and friendly, the number of incidents involving cruel Machokes is rising.

248.name: Machamp

attacks.name: Seething Anger
attacks.text: Flip a number of coins equal to the number of damage counters on Machamp. This attack does 20 damage plus 10 more damage for each heads.

attacks.name: Fling
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and switches it with the Defending Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

248.flavor: Using its amazing muscles, it throws powerful punches that can knock its victim clear over the horizon.

249.name: Machamp

attacks.name: Strikes Back
attacks.text: Whenever your opponent's attack damages Machamp (even if Machamp is Knocked Out), this power does 10 damage to the attacking Pokemon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance.) This power can't be used if Machamp is already Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed when your opponent attacks.

249.flavor: Its four ruggedly developed arms can launch a flurry of 1,000 punches in just two seconds.

250.name: Dark Machamp

attacks.name: Fling
attacks.text: Your opponent shuffles his or her Active Pokemon and all cards attached to it into his or her deck. This attack can't be used if your opponent has no Benched Pokemon.

250.flavor: It is almost impossible to defend against a Machamp's four powerful arms.

251.name: Geodude

attacks.name: Harden
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, if this Pokemon would be damaged by an attack, prevent that attack's damage done to this Pokemon if that damage is 20 or less.

251.flavor: Found in fields and mountains. Mistaking them for boulders, people often step or trip on them.

252.name: Geodude

attacks.name: Stone Barrage
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. This attack does 10 damage times the number of heads.

252.flavor: Its round form makes it easy to pick up. Opponents can grab and throw Geodude during battle.

253.name: Graveler

attacks.name: Boulder Smash
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. For each heads, put 1 damage counter on 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon.

253.flavor: Rolls down slopes to move. It rolls over any obstacle without slowing or changing its direction.

254.name: Graveler

attacks.name: Rock Cannon
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

attacks.name: Earthquake
attacks.text: Does 10 damage to each of your Benched Pokemon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

254.flavor: Rolls down slopes to move. It rolls over any obstacle without slowing or changing its direction.

255.name: Graveler

attacks.name: Harden
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, whenever 30 or less damage is done to Graveler (after applying Weakness and Resistance), prevent that damage. (Any other effects of attacks still happen.)

255.flavor: While hiking on mountain trails Graveler may come rolling down there.

256.name: Golem

attacks.name: Selfdestruct
attacks.text: Does 20 damage to each Pokemon on each player's Bench. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.) Golem does 100 damage to itself.

256.flavor: It is enclosed in a hard shell that is as rugged as slabs of rock. It sheds skin once a year to grow larger.

257.name: Golem

attacks.name: Rock Blast
attacks.text: You may discard up to 5 Fighting Energy cards attached to Golem. For each Fighting Energy you discarded, choose 1 of your opponent's Pokemon and this attack does 20 damage to it. (You may choose the same Pokemon more than once.) Don't apply Weakness or Resistance.

257.flavor: Its body is made from tough granite. Even dynamite cannot cause any damage.

258.name: Onix

attacks.name: Harden
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, whenever 30 or less damage is done to Onix (after applying Weakness and Resistance), prevent that damage. (Any other effects of attacks still happen.)

258.flavor: It usually lives underground. It searches for food while boring its way through the ground at 80 kilometers per hour.

259.name: Onix

attacks.name: Bind
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Rock Seal
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon can't retreat during your opponent's next turn.

259.flavor: As it grows, the stone portions of its body harden to become similar to a diamond, but colored black.

260.name: Cubone

attacks.name: Snivel
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon attacks Cubone during your opponent's next turn, any damage done by the attack is reduced by 20 (after applying Weakness and Resistance). (Benching either Pokemon ends this effect.)

attacks.name: Rage
attacks.text: Does 10 damage plus 10 more damage for each damage counter on Cubone.

260.flavor: It wears the skull of its dead mother on its head. When it becomes lonesome, it is said to cry loudly.

261.name: Cubone

attacks.name: Bone Toss
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 damage to the Defending Pokemon. If tails, this attack does 10 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

261.flavor: Because it never removes its skull helmet, no one has ever seen this Pokemon's real face.

262.name: Marowak

attacks.name: Bonemerang
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads.

attacks.name: Call for Friend
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Fighting Basic Pokemon card and put it onto your Bench. Shuffle your deck afterward. (You can't use this attack if your Bench is full.)

262.flavor: Small and weak, this Pokemon is adept with its bone club. It has grown more vicious over the ages.

263.name: Marowak

attacks.name: Bone Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon can't attack during your opponent's next turn.

attacks.name: Wail
attacks.text: Each player fills his or her bench with Basic Pokemon chosen at random from his or her deck. If a player has fewer Basic Pokemon than that in his or her deck, he or she chooses all of them. Each player shuffles his or her deck afterward.

263.flavor: The bone it holds is its key weapon. It throws the bone skillfully like a boomerang to stun targets.

264.name: Dark Marowak

attacks.name: Bone Headbutt
attacks.text: Does a randomly selected amount of damage (0, 10, or 20) to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon chosen at random. Then, the Defending Pokemon is switched with a Benched Pokemon chosen at random.

264.flavor: The impact of its headbutt was so immeasurable, it was flung over even the bench.

265.name: Hitmonlee

attacks.name: Double Kick
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads.

attacks.name: Rolling Kick
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

265.flavor: When in a hurry, its legs lengthen progressively. It runs smoothly with extra long, loping strides.

266.name: Hitmonlee

attacks.name: Stretch Kick
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, choose 1 of them and this attack does 20 damage to it. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

266.flavor: The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.

267.name: Hitmonchan

attacks.name: Mach Punch
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 10 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

267.flavor: While apparently doing nothing, it fires punches in lightning fast volleys that are impossible to see.

268.name: Hitmonchan
268.flavor: The spirit of a pro boxer has infused this Pokemon. It throws punches that are faster than a bullet train.

269.name: Rhyhorn

attacks.name: Leer
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon can't attack Rhyhorn during your opponent's next turn. (Benching either Pokemon ends this effect.)

269.flavor: Strong, but not too bright, this Pokemon can shatter even a skyscraper with its charging tackles.

270.name: Rhydon

attacks.name: Mountain Breaker
attacks.text: Discard the top 5 cards of your deck. If any of those cards are Fighting Energy cards, put them into your hand.

attacks.name: One-Two Strike
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

270.flavor: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 2000 degrees.

271.name: Rhydon

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.text: Rhydon does 20 damage to itself. If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and switches it with the Defending Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon. Switch the Pokemon even if Rhydon is knocked out.)

271.flavor: It begins walking on its hind legs after evolution. It can punch holes through boulders with its horn.

272.name: Kabuto

attacks.name: Kabuto Armor
attacks.text: Whenever an attack (even your own) does damage to Kabuto (after applying Weakness and Resistance), that attack only does half the damage to Kabuto (rounded down to the nearest 10). (Any other effects of attacks still happen.) This power stops working while Kabuto is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

272.flavor: This Pokemon was regenerated from the fossil of an ancient creature. It protects itself with a hard shell.

273.name: Kabuto

attacks.name: Fossilize
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may flip a coin. If heads, return all Evolution cards from 1 of your Pokemon in play that evolves from Mysterious Fossil to your hand. This power can't be used if this Pokemon is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Sharp Claws
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 more damage.

273.flavor: A Pokemon that was resurrected from a fossil found in what was once the ocean floor eons ago.

274.name: Kabutops

attacks.name: Absorb
attacks.text: Remove a number of damage counters from Kabutops equal to half the damage done to the Defending Pokemon (after applying Weakness and Resistance) (rounded up to the nearest 10). If Kabutops has fewer damage counters than that, remove all of them.

274.flavor: It swims freely through water. It catches prey with its scythe-like arms and drains the victim's fluids.

275.name: Aerodactyl

attacks.name: Prehistoric Power
attacks.text: No more Evolution cards can be played. This power stops working while Aerodactyl is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

275.flavor: It was regenerated from a dinosaur's genetic matter that was found in amber. It flies with high-pitched cries.

276.name: Aerodactyl

attacks.name: Supersonic
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Tailspin Attack
attacks.text: This Pokemon does 10 damage to itself. Don't apply Weakness and Resistance.

276.flavor: A ferocious, prehistoric Pokemon that goes for the enemy's throat with its serrated saw-like fangs.

277.name: Abra

attacks.name: Psychic Beam
attacks.text: Does 10 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokemon. Don't apply Weakness or Resistance.

277.flavor: Using its ability to read minds, it will sense impending danger and teleport to safety.

278.name: Abra

attacks.name: Psyshock
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

278.flavor: It sleeps for 18 hours a day. It uses a variety of extrasensory powers even while asleep.

279.name: Abra

attacks.name: Vanish
attacks.text: Shuffle Abra into your deck. (Discard all cards attached to Abra.)

attacks.name: Psyshock
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

279.flavor: It teleports itself away from danger, making it difficult to capture.

280.name: Kadabra

attacks.name: Recover
attacks.text: Discard 1 Psychic Energy card attached to Kadabra in order to use this attack. Remove all damage counters from Kadabra.

280.flavor: It happened one morning - a boy with extrasensory powers awoke in bed transformed into Kadabra.
280.from: Base Set and Base Set 2 prints

281.name: Kadabra

attacks.name: Psycho Panic
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon is Psychic, this attack's base damage is doubled.

attacks.name: Blink
attacks.text: If an attack damages this Pokemon during your opponent's next turn, flip a coin. If heads, prevent that damage. (Any other effects of attacks still happen.)

281.flavor: It emits special alpha waves from its body that induce headaches just by being close by.

282.name: Dark Kadabra

attacks.name: Matter Exchange
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may discard a card from your hand in order to draw a card. This power can't be used if Dark Kadabra is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Mind Shock
attacks.text: Don't apply Weakness or Resistance for this attack. (Any other effects that would happen after applying Weakness and Resistance still happen.)

282.flavor: Some people say that Kadabras are responsible for many of the mysterious events reported in the news.

283.name: Alakazam

attacks.name: Damage Swap
attacks.text: As often as you like during your turn (before your attack), you may move 1 damage counter from 1 of your Pokemon to another as long as you don't Knock Out that Pokemon. This power can't be used if Alakazam is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Confuse Ray
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

283.flavor: It does not like physical attacks very much. Instead, it freely uses extra-sensory powers to defeat foes.

284.name: Alakazam

attacks.name: Psycho Panic
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon is Psychic, this attack's base damage is doubled.

attacks.name: Trans Damage
attacks.text: Discard all Energy cards attached to Alakazam. Move all damage counters from Alakazam to the Defending Pokemon.

284.flavor: Its brain can outperform a supercomputer. Its intelligence quotient is said to be 5000.

285.name: Dark Alakazam

attacks.name: Teleport Blast
attacks.text: You may switch Dark Alakazam with 1 of your Benched Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

attacks.name: Mind Shock
attacks.text: Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for this attack. (Any other effects that would happen after applying Weakness and Resistance still happen.)

285.flavor: Almost as if it were being controlled by something else, it never changes expressions, even in the middle of battle.

286.name: Slowpoke

attacks.name: Amnesia
attacks.text: Choose 1 of the Defending Pokemon's attacks. That Pokemon can't use that attack during your opponent's next turn.

286.flavor: It is always in a daze, and no one knows what it is thinking about. It uses its tail as bait when fishing.

287.name: Slowpoke

attacks.name: Afternoon Nap
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Psychic Energy card and attach it to Slowpoke. Shuffle your deck afterward.

287.flavor: Although it knows how to fish, no other intelligent behavior has been detected in it.

288.name: Slowpoke

attacks.name: Spacing Out
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, remove a damage counter from Slowpoke. This attack can't be used if Slowpoke has no damage counters on it.

attacks.name: Scavenge
attacks.text: Discard 1 Psychic Energy card attached to Slowpoke in order to use this attack. Put a Trainer card from your discard pile into your hand.

288.flavor: It is always vacantly lost in thought, but no one knows what it is thinking about. It is good at fishing with its tail.

289.name: Slowbro

attacks.name: Strange Behavior
attacks.text: As often as you like during your turn (before your attack), you may move 1 damage counter from 1 of your Pokemon to Slowbro as long as you don't Knock Out Slowbro. This power can't be used if Slowbro is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Psyshock
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

289.flavor: When a Slowpoke went hunting in the sea, its tail was bitten by a Shellder. That made it evolve into Slowbro.

290.name: Slowbro

attacks.name: Big Yawn
attacks.text: Both the Defending Pokemon and this Pokemon are now Asleep.

attacks.name: Big Snore
attacks.text: You can only use this attack if this Pokemon is Asleep.

290.flavor: The Shellder that is latched onto Slowpoke's tail is said to feed on the host's left-over scraps.

291.name: Dark Slowbro

attacks.name: Reel In
attacks.text: When you play Dark Slowbro from your hand, choose up to 3 Basic Pokemon and/or Evolution cards from your discard pile and put them into your hand.

attacks.name: Fickle Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

291.flavor: It loves nothing better than to be left alone, and so sometimes ends up being manipulated by unscrupulous people.

292.name: Gastly

attacks.name: Sleeping Gas
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Destiny Bond
attacks.text: Discard 1 Psychic Energy card attached to Gastly in order to use this attack. If a Pokemon Knocks Out Gastly during your opponent's next turn, Knock Out that Pokemon.

292.flavor: A being that exists as a thin gas. It can topple an Indian elephant by enveloping the prey in two seconds.

293.name: Gastly

attacks.name: Spookify
attacks.text: Your opponent can't play Trainer cards from his or her hand during his or her next turn.

attacks.name: Fade to Black
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

293.flavor: Almost invisible, this gaseous Pokemon cloaks the target and puts it to sleep without notice.

294.name: Gastly

attacks.name: Lick
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Energy Conversion
attacks.text: Put up to 2 Energy cards from your discard pile into your hand. Gastly does 10 damage to itself.

294.flavor: A mysterious Pokemon. Some say it is a lifeform from another dimension, while others believe it is formed from smog.

295.name: Haunter

attacks.name: Nightmare
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Transparency
attacks.text: Whenever an attack does anything to Haunter, flip a coin. If heads, prevent all effects of that attack, including damage, done to Haunter. This power stops working while Haunter is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

295.flavor: If you get the feeling of being watched in darkness when nobody is around, Haunter is there.

296.name: Haunter

attacks.name: Hypnosis
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Dream Eater
attacks.text: You can't use this attack unless the Defending Pokemon is Asleep.

296.flavor: If you get the feeling of being watched in darkness when nobody is around, Haunter is there.

297.name: Haunter

attacks.name: Eerie Light
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Grudge
attacks.text: Does 20 damage plus 10 more damage for each Prize card your opponent has taken.

297.flavor: Because of its ability to slip through block walls, it is said to be from another dimension.

298.name: Haunter

attacks.name: Poltergeist
attacks.text: Look at your opponent's hand. This attack does 10 damage times the number of Trainer cards your opponent has in his or her hand.

attacks.name: Bad Dreams
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep. If tails, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

298.flavor: Because of its ability to slip through block walls, it is said to be from another dimension.

attacks.name: Bother
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, shuffle a randomly selected Trainer card from your opponent's hand back into his or her deck.

300.name: Gengar

attacks.name: Curse
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may move 1 damage counter from 1 of your opponent's Pokemon to another (even if it would Knock Out the other Pokemon). This power can't be used if Gengar is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Dark Mind
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, choose 1 of them and this attack does 10 damage to it. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

300.flavor: It is said to emerge from darkness to steal the lives of those who become lost in mountains.

301.name: Gengar

attacks.name: Power of Darkness
attacks.text: When you play Gengar from your hand, you may flip a coin. If heads, choose 1 of your opponent's Pokemon. Your opponent returns that Pokemon and all cards attached to it to his or her hand.

attacks.name: Psy Horror
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep. If tails, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

301.flavor: Under a full moon, this Pokemon likes to mimic the shadows of people and laugh at their fright.

302.name: Dark Gengar

attacks.name: Play Tricks
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may choose to have all damage counters on your opponent's Pokemon randomly rearranged (your opponent's Pokemon cannot be knocked out in this way). This Power can't be used if Dark Gengar is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Push Aside
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent shuffles a random Pokemon and all cards attached to it into his or her deck.

302.flavor: If a Pokemon was to disappear into darkness, it would certainly have to be the work of Gengar.

303.name: Drowzee

attacks.name: Long-Distance Hypnosis
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep; if tails, your Active Pokemon is now Asleep. The power can't be used if Drowzee is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Nightmare
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

303.flavor: Not popular with girls because of its attitude. Can often be heard muttering to itself in a low voice.

304.name: Drowzee

attacks.name: Confuse Ray
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

304.flavor: A descendant of the legendary animal baku, which is said to eat dreams. It is skilled at hypnotism.

305.name: Hypno

attacks.name: Puppet Master
attacks.text: If a Clefairy Doll is your Active Pokemon, it may use any of this Pokemon's attacks as long as this Pokemon has enough Energy cards attached to it to pay for that attack's Energy cost. (The Clefairy Doll can make that attack even if it does not have the appropriate number or type of Energy attached to it necessary to make the attack.)

attacks.name: Mind Shock
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance.

305.flavor: When it locks eyes with an enemy, it will use a mix of psi moves such as Hypnosis and Confusion.

306.name: Hypno

attacks.name: Prophecy
attacks.text: Look at up to 3 cards from the top of either player's deck and rearrange them as you like.

attacks.name: Dark Mind
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, choose 1 of them and this attack does 10 damage to it. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

306.flavor: It carries a pendulum-like device. There once was an incident in which it took away a child it hypnotized.

307.name: Dark Hypno

attacks.name: Bench Manipulation
attacks.text: Your opponent flips a number of coins equal to the number of Pokemon on his or her Bench. This attack does 20 damage times the number of tails. Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for this attack. (Any other effects that would happen after applying Weakness and Resistance still happen.)

307.flavor: Carries a pendulum with it always. Sometimes appears near less-traveled roads and schools at dusk.

308.name: Mr. Mime

attacks.name: Dampening Shield
attacks.text: As long as this Pokemon is on your Bench, Pokemon in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Weakness or Resistance.

attacks.name: Juggling
attacks.text: Flip 4 coins. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

308.flavor: If interrupted while miming, it will slap around the enemy with its broad hands.

309.name: Mr. Mime

attacks.name: Invisible Wall
attacks.text: Whenever an attack (including your own) does 30 or more damage to Mr. Mime (after applying Weakness and Resistance), prevent that damage. (Any other effects of attacks still happen.) This power can't be used if Mr. Mime is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Meditate
attacks.text: Does 10 damage plus 10 more damage for each damage counter on the Defending Pokemon.

309.flavor: It is adept at conning people. It is said to be able to create walls out of thin air by miming.

310.name: Jynx

attacks.name: Ice Punch
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Cold Breath
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

310.flavor: It seductively wiggles its hips as it walks. It can cause people to dance in unison with it.

311.name: Jynx

attacks.name: Doubleslap
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 10 damage times the number of heads.

attacks.name: Meditate
attacks.text: Does 20 damage plus 10 more damage for each damage counter on the Defending Pokemon.

311.flavor: It speaks using a language that sounds human. Research is under way to determine what is being said.

312.name: Jynx

attacks.name: Double Slap
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

312.flavor: Appears to move to a rhythm of its own, as if it were dancing. It wiggles its hips as it walks.

313.name: Mewtwo

attacks.name: Energy Control
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, choose a basic Energy card attached to 1 of your opponent's Pokemon and attach it to another of your opponent's Pokemon of your choice.

attacks.name: Telekinesis
attacks.text: Choose 1 of your opponent's Pokemon. This attack does 30 damage to that Pokemon. Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for this attack. (Any other effects that would happen after applying Weakness and Resistance still happen.)

313.flavor: A scientist created this Pokemon after years of horrific gene-splicing and DNA engineering experiments.

314.name: Mewtwo

attacks.name: Psychic
attacks.text: Does 10 damage plus 10 more damage for each Energy card attached to the Defending Pokemon.

attacks.name: Barrier
attacks.text: Discard 1 Psychic Energy card attached to Mewtwo in order to use this attack. During your opponent's next turn, prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to Mewtwo.

314.flavor: A Pokemon whose genetic code was repeatedly recombined for research. It turned vicious as a result.

315.name: Mewtwo

attacks.name: Psycrush
attacks.text: Does 10 damage times the total number of Psychic Energy cards attached to all of your opponent's Pokemon.

315.flavor: It was created by a scientist after years of horrific gene splicing and DNA engineering experiments.

316.name: Mewtwo

attacks.name: Energy Absorption
attacks.text: Choose up to 2 Energy cards from your discard pile and attach them to Mewtwo.

316.flavor: As a result of a reclassified gene of Pokemon, it gave birth to an unpredicted rogue Pokemon.

317.name: Mewtwo

attacks.name: Energy Absorption
attacks.text: Choose up to 2 Energy cards from your discard pile and attach them to Mewtwo.

317.flavor: As a result of a reclassified gene of Pokemon, it gave birth to an unpredicted rogue Pokemon.

318.name: Mewtwo

attacks.name: Complete Recovery
attacks.text: Discard all Energy cards attached to this Pokemon. Then, remove all damage counters and markers from this Pokemon and this Pokemon is no longer Poisoned or Confused.

attacks.name: Psycho Blast
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard 1 Energy card attached to the Defending Pokemon.

318.flavor: It was created by a scientist after years of horrific gene splicing and DNA engineering experiments.
