319.name: Team GR's Mewtwo

attacks.name: Dark Wave
attacks.text: Whenever 1 of your Pokemon with Dark in its name does damage to any Pokemon with an attack, flip a coin. If heads, flip another coin. If the second coin is heads, that attack does 20 more damage. If the second coin is tails, that attack does 10 more damage. If you have more than 1 Team GR's Mewtwo in play, use only 1 Dark Wave for an attack. This power stops working while Team GR's Mewtwo is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Dark Amplification
attacks.text: Flip a number of coins equal to the number of Pokemon with Dark in their names on your Bench. This attack does 20 damage plus 20 damage times the number of heads.

319.flavor: It's said to possess the power to control Dark Pokemon. Consequently, its body is never seen.

320.name: Mew

attacks.name: Neutral Shield
attacks.text: Prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to Mew by Evolved Pokemon. You can't use this power if Mew is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Psyshock
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

320.flavor: So rare that it is still said to be a mirage by many experts. Only a few people have seen it worldwide.

321.name: Mew

attacks.name: Mystery Attack
attacks.text: Does a random amount of damage to the Defending Pokemon and may cause a random effect to the Defending Pokemon.

321.flavor: A Pokemon of South America that was thought to have been extinct. It is very intelligent and learns any move.

322.name: Mew

attacks.name: Psywave
attacks.text: Does 10 damage times the number of Energy cards attached to the Defending Pokemon.

attacks.name: Devolution Beam
attacks.text: Choose an evolved Pokemon (your own or your opponent's). Return the highest Stage Evolution card on that Pokemon to its player's hand. That Pokemon is no longer Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned, or anything else that might be the result of an attack (just as if you had evolved it).

322.flavor: So rare that it is still said to be a mirage by many experts. Only a few people have seen it worldwide.

323.name: Pidgey

attacks.name: Whirlwind
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and switches it with the Defending Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

323.flavor: Does not like to fight. It hides in tall grass and so on, foraging for food such as small bugs.
323.from: Base Set and Base Set 2 prints

324.name: Pidgey

attacks.name: Quick Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

324.flavor: A common sight in forests and woods. It flaps its wings at ground level to kick up blinding sand.

325.name: Pidgeotto

attacks.name: Whirlwind
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and switches it with the Defending Pokemon. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

attacks.name: Mirror Move
attacks.text: If Pidgeotto was attacked last turn, do the final result of that attack on Pidgeotto to the Defending Pokemon.

325.flavor: The claws on its feet are well developed. It can carry prey such as an Exeggcute to its nest over 100 kilometers away.
325.from: Base Set and Base Set 2 prints

326.name: Pidgeotto

attacks.name: Twister
attacks.text: Unless this attack Knocks Out the Defending Pokemon, flip a coin. If heads, return all Trainer cards and Energy cards attached to the Defending Pokemon to your opponent's hand.

attacks.name: Fly
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing. If heads, prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to this Pokemon during your opponent's next turn.

326.flavor: Very protective of its sprawling territory, this Pokemon will fiercely peck at any intruder.

327.name: Pidgeot

attacks.name: Slicing Wind
attacks.text: Does 30 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokemon chosen at random. Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for this attack. (Any other effects that would happen after applying Weakness and Resistance still happen.)

attacks.name: Gale
attacks.text: Switch Pidgeot with 1 of your Benched Pokemon chosen at random. If your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, switch the Defending Pokemon with 1 of them chosen at random. (Do the damage before switching the Pokemon.)

327.flavor: It spreads its gorgeous wings widely to intimidate enemies. It races through the skies at Mach-2 speed.

328.name: Pidgeot

attacks.name: Hurricane
attacks.text: Unless this attack Knocks Out the Defending Pokemon, return the Defending Pokemon and all cards attached to it to your opponent's hand.

328.flavor: It spreads its gorgeous wings widely to intimidate enemies. It races through the skies at Mach-2 speed.

329.name: Rattata
329.flavor: Its fangs are long and very sharp. They grow continuously, so it gnaws on hard things to whittle them down.

330.name: Rattata

attacks.name: Trickery
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may switch 1 of your Prizes with the top card of your deck. This power can't be used if Rattata is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Quick Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 10 damage plus 10 more damage; if tails, this attack does 10 damage.

330.flavor: Loves to eat walnuts and acorns and nuts, processed goods, cheese, and milk.

331.name: Rattata

attacks.name: Tail Whip
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon can't attack during your opponent's next turn.

331.flavor: Bites anything when it attacks. Small and very quick, it is a common sight in many places.

332.name: Raticate

attacks.name: Super Fang
attacks.text: Does damage to the Defending Pokemon equal to half the Defending Pokemon's remaining HP (rounded up to the nearest 10).

332.flavor: Its rear feet have three toes each. They are webbed, enabling it to swim across rivers.

333.name: Dark Raticate

attacks.name: Hyper Fang
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

333.flavor: A Raticate's front teeth are incredibly powerful; it can destroy a two-story house with them in 5 minutes.

334.name: Spearow
334.flavor: Inept at flying high. However, it can fly around very fast to protect its territory.

335.name: Spearow

attacks.name: Fury Attack
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 10 damage times the number of heads.

335.flavor: Eats bugs in grassy areas. It has to flap its short wings at high speed to stay airborne.

336.name: Spearow

attacks.name: Mirror Move
attacks.text: If Spearow was attacked last turn, do the final result of that attack on Spearow to the Defending Pokemon.

336.flavor: It busily flits around here and there. It is physically weak, but uses Parrot Mimicry to prove a difficult foe.

337.name: Fearow

attacks.name: Quick Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

attacks.name: Drill Descent
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

337.flavor: With its huge and magnificent wings, it can keep aloft without ever having to land for rest.

338.name: Fearow

attacks.name: Agility
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all effects of attacks, including damage, done to Fearow.

338.flavor: Its great wings can keep it aloft in the sky. It can remain flying a whole day without landing.

339.name: Dark Fearow

attacks.name: Fly High
attacks.text: During your next turn, Dark Fearow's Drill Dive attack's base damage is doubled.

attacks.name: Drill Dive
attacks.text: During your next turn, Dark Fearow can't attack or retreat.

339.flavor: It suddenly appears from the clouds with a swooping attack that is difficult to dodge.

340.name: Clefairy

attacks.name: Sing
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Metronome
attacks.text: Choose 1 of the Defending Pokemon's attacks. Metronome copies that attack except for its Energy costs and anything else required in order to use that attack, such as discarding Energy cards. (No matter what type the Defending Pokemon is, Clefairy's type is still Colorless.)

340.flavor: Its adorable appearance makes it popular as a pet. However, it is rare and difficult to find.

341.name: Clefairy

attacks.name: Follow Me
attacks.text: Switch the Defending Pokemon with 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon.

attacks.name: Shining Fingers
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

341.flavor: Its magical and cute appeal has many admirers. It is rare and found only in certain areas.

342.name: Clefable

attacks.name: Metronome
attacks.text: Choose 1 of the Defending Pokemon's attacks. Metronome copies that attack except for its Energy costs and anything else required in order to use that attack, such as discarding Energy cards. (No matter what type the Defending Pokemon is, Clefable's type is still Colorless.)

attacks.name: Minimize
attacks.text: All damage done by attacks to Clefable during your opponent's next turn is reduced by 20 (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

342.flavor: It has an acute sense of hearing. It can easily hear a pin being dropped nearly 1 kilometer away.

343.name: Dark Clefable

attacks.name: Darkness Veil
attacks.text: If your Dark Pokemon is the Active Pokemon, all damage from attacks done to it during your opponent's turn is reduced by a random number (0, 10, 20). This Power stops working if Dark Clefable is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Dark Song
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep, and this attack also does 10 damage to each of your opponent's Benched Pokemon that isn't Dark Pokemon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

343.flavor: If it senses anyone nearby, it will protect its friends with a mysterious power that only fairies possess.

344.name: Jigglypuff

attacks.name: First Aid
attacks.text: Remove 1 damage counter from Jigglypuff.

attacks.name: Double-edge
attacks.text: Jigglypuff does 20 damage to itself.

344.flavor: When its huge eyes light up, it sings a mysteriously soothing melody that lulls its enemies to sleep.

345.name: Jigglypuff

attacks.name: Friendship Song
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, put a Basic Pokemon chosen at random from your deck onto your Bench. (You can't use this attack if your bench is full.)

attacks.name: Expand
attacks.text: All damage done to Jigglypuff during your opponent's next turn is reduced by 10 (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

345.flavor: When its huge eyes light up, it sings a mysteriously soothing melody that lulls its enemies to sleep.

346.name: Jigglypuff

attacks.name: Lullaby
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

346.flavor: If it does not like something, it will puff up and swell like a balloon.

347.name: Wigglytuff

attacks.name: Lullaby
attacks.text: The Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Do the Wave
attacks.text: Does 10 damage plus 10 more damage for each of your Benched Pokemon.

347.flavor: Its fur is extremely fine, dense, and supple. The exquisitely pleasant fur conveys an image of luxury.

348.name: Wigglytuff

attacks.name: Helping Hand
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), if this Pokemon is on your Bench, you may flip a coin. If heads, remove 1 Special Condition from your Active Pokemon.

attacks.name: Expand
attacks.text: All damage done to this Pokemon by attacks during your opponent's next turn is reduced by 10 (after applying Weakness and Resistance.)

348.flavor: The body is soft and rubbery. When angered, it will suck in air and inflate itself to an enormous size.

349.name: Meowth

attacks.name: Coin Hurl
attacks.text: Choose 1 of your opponent's Pokemon and flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 damage to that Pokemon. Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for this attack. (Any other effects that would happen after applying Weakness and Resistance still happen.)

349.flavor: A popular Pokemon that earns money for its owner with its "Pay Day" ability.

350.name: Meowth

attacks.name: Cat Punch
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 damage. If tails and if your opponent has any Benched Pokemon, he or she chooses 1 of them and this attack does 20 damage to it. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokemon.)

350.flavor: Adores circular objects. Wanders the street on a nightly basis to look for dropped loose change.

351.name: Meowth

attacks.name: Clear Profit
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. For each heads, draw a card.

351.flavor: Adores circular objects. Wanders the street on a nightly basis to look for dropped loose change.

352.name: Meowth

attacks.name: Pay Day
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, draw a card.

352.flavor: All it does is sleep during the daytime. At night, it patrols its territory with its eyes aglow.

353.name: Meowth

attacks.name: Fury Swipes
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 10 damage times the number of heads.

353.flavor: Appears to be more active at night. It loves round and shiny things. It can't stop from picking them up.

354.name: Persian

attacks.name: Pounce
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon attacks Persian during your opponent's next turn, any damage done by the attack is reduced by 10 (after applying Weakness and Resistance).(Benching either Pokemon ends this effect.)

354.flavor: Has a vicious temperament. Beware if it raises its tail straight up. It is a signal that it is about to pounce and bite.

355.name: Dark Persian

attacks.name: Fascinate
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, choose 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon and switch it with the Defending Pokemon. This attack can't be used if your opponent has no Benched Pokemon.

attacks.name: Poison Claws
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

355.flavor: Popular with women because of its beautiful fur. The leader of the Rockets keeps one as a pet.
355.from: Team Rocket and Legendary Collection prints

356.name: Dark Persian

attacks.name: Fascinate
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, choose 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon and switch it with the Defending Pokemon. This attack can't be used if your opponent has no Benched Pokemon.

attacks.name: Poison Claws
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Poisoned.

356.flavor: Popular with women because of its beautiful fur. The leader of the Rockets keeps one as a pet.
356.from: Team Rocket and Legendary Collection prints

357.name: Farfetch'd

attacks.name: Leek Slap
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing. Either way, you can't use this attack again as long as Farfetch'd stays in play (even putting Farfetch'd on the Bench won't let you use it again).

357.flavor: It always walks about with a plant stalk clamped in its beak. The stalk is used for building its nest.

358.name: Farfetch'd

attacks.name: Leek Slap
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing. Either way, you can't use this attack again as long as Farfetch'd stays in play (even putting Farfetch'd on the Bench won't let you use it again).

358.flavor: It always walks about with a plant stalk clamped in its beak. The stalk is used for building its nest.

359.name: Doduo

attacks.name: Growl
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, any damage done by attacks from the Defending Pokemon is reduced by 10 (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

359.flavor: A bird that makes up for its poor flying with its fast foot speed. Leaves giant footprints.

360.name: Doduo

attacks.name: Fury Attack
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 10 damage times the number of heads.

360.flavor: A two-headed Pokemon that was discovered as a sudden mutation. It runs at a pace of over 100 kilometers per hour.

361.name: Dodrio

attacks.name: Tri Attack
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

361.flavor: Uses its three brains to execute complex plans. While two heads sleep, one head is said to stay awake.

362.name: Dodrio

attacks.name: Retreat Aid
attacks.text: As long as Dodrio is Benched, pay less to retreat your Active Pokemon.

attacks.name: Rage
attacks.text: Does 10 damage plus 10 more damage for each damage counter on Dodrio.

362.flavor: A curious species that is rarely found. The three heads represent the emotions of joy, sadness, and anger.

363.name: Lickitung

attacks.name: Lick
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Stomp
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 10 more damage.

363.flavor: Its tongue can be extended like a chameleon's. It leaves a tingling sensation when it licks enemies.

364.name: Lickitung

attacks.name: Tongue Wrap
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Supersonic
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

364.flavor: Its tongue is twice the length of its body. It can be moved like an arm for grabbing food and attacking.

365.name: Chansey

attacks.name: Sing
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Double Slap
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

365.flavor: A rare and elusive Pokemon that is said to bring happiness to those who manage to get it.

366.name: Chansey

attacks.name: Scrunch
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, prevent all damage done to Chansey during your opponent's next turn. (Any other effects of attacks still happen.)

attacks.name: Double-edge
attacks.text: Chansey does 80 damage to itself.

366.flavor: It lays several eggs a day. The eggs are apparently rich in nutrients and extremely delicious.

367.name: Kangaskhan

attacks.name: Tail Drop
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. If either of them is tails, this attack does nothing.

367.flavor: The infant rarely ventures out of its mother's protective pouch until it is 3 years old.

368.name: Kangaskhan

attacks.name: Dizzy Punch
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 10 damage times the number of heads.

368.flavor: The infant rarely ventures out of its mother's protective pouch until it is 3 years old.

369.name: Kangaskhan

attacks.name: Fetch
attacks.text: Draw a card.

attacks.name: Comet Punch
attacks.text: Flip 4 coins. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

369.flavor: The female raises its offspring in a pouch on its belly. It is skilled at attacking using Comet Punch.

370.name: Tauros

attacks.name: Stomp
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 damage plus 10 more damage; if tails, this attack does 20 damage.

attacks.name: Rampage
attacks.text: Does 20 damage plus 10 more damage for each damage counter on Tauros. Flip a coin. If tails, Tauros is now Confused (after doing damage).

370.flavor: When it is about to tackle, it whips its body repeatedly with two of its tails.

371.name: Tauros

attacks.name: Kicking and Stamping
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 10 more damage. If tails, your opponent switches the Defending Pokemon with 1 of his or her Benched Pokemon.

371.flavor: When it targets an enemy, it charges furiously while whipping its body with its long tails.

372.name: Ditto

attacks.name: Morph
attacks.text: Remove all damage counters from Ditto. For the rest of the game, replace Ditto with a copy of a Basic Pokemon Card (other than Ditto) chosen at random from your deck. Ditto is no longer Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or anything else that might be the result of an attack (just as if you had evolved it).

372.flavor: When it spots an enemy, its body transforms into an almost perfect copy of its opponent.

373.name: Eevee

attacks.name: Lunge
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

373.flavor: Its genetic code is irregular. It may mutate if it is exposed to radiation from element stones.

374.name: Eevee

attacks.name: Sand-attack
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon tries to attack during your opponent's next turn, your opponent flips a coin. If tails, that attack does nothing.

374.flavor: A rare and unique Pokemon about which little is known, as few have been captured.

375.name: Eevee

attacks.name: Tail Wag
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon can't attack Eevee during your opponent's next turn. (Benching either Pokemon ends this effect.)

attacks.name: Quick Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 10 damage plus 20 more damage; if tails, this attack does 10 damage.

375.flavor: A rare Pokemon that has the potential to evolve into three different Pokemon.

376.name: Porygon

attacks.name: Conversion 1
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon has a Weakness, you may change it to a type of your choice other than Colorless.

attacks.name: Conversion 2
attacks.text: Change Porygon's Resistance to a type of your choice other than Colorless.

376.flavor: Using the most advanced technologies, scientists finally succeeded in making the first artificial Pokemon.

377.name: Porygon

attacks.name: 3-D Attack
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 10 damage times the number of heads.

attacks.name: Conversion 2
attacks.text: Change this Pokemon's Resistance to a type of your choice other than Colorless.

377.flavor: A Pokemon that consists entirely of programming code. Capable of moving freely in cyberspace.

378.name: Porygon

attacks.name: Conversion 1
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon has a Weakness, you may change it to a type of your choice other than Colorless. (Benching either Pokemon ends this effect.)

attacks.name: Psybeam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Confused.

378.flavor: More and more people play the slots every day, trying to win a Porygon.

379.name: Cool Porygon

attacks.name: Texture Magic
attacks.text: You may change Cool Porygon's Resistance to a type of your choice other than Colorless. If the Defending Pokemon has a Weakness, you may change it to a type of your choice other than Colorless. (Benching either Pokemon ends the effect on that Pokemon.)

attacks.name: 3-D Attack
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 20 damage times the number of heads.

379.flavor: Its body is made of program. It has the ability to move at will through electronic space.

380.name: Snorlax

attacks.name: Thick Skinned
attacks.text: Snorlax can't become Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned. This power can't be used if Snorlax is already Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Body Slam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

380.flavor: It is not satisfied unless it eats over 400 kilograms of food every day. After eating, it falls asleep.

381.name: Snorlax

attacks.name: Guard
attacks.text: As long as Snorlax is your Active Pokemon, the Defending Pokemon can't Retreat. This power stops working when Snorlax is affected by a Special Condition.

attacks.name: Roll Over
attacks.text: Snorlax is now Asleep. Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

381.flavor: Loves to doze, it will often fall asleep in the middle of roads.

382.name: Hungry Snorlax

attacks.name: Eat
attacks.text: Put 1 Food counter on Hungry Snorlax. You can't use this attack if Hungry Snorlax already has 2 Food counters on it.

attacks.name: Rollout
attacks.text: You may remove any number of Food counters from Hungry Snorlax. If you do, this attack does 20 damage plus 30 damage for each Food counter you removed. If you don't, this attack does 20 damage.

382.flavor: A lazy Pokemon that gets continually fatter by sticking to a cycle of sleeping and eating. Awake only when it eats.

383.name: Dratini
383.flavor: Even the young can exceed 2 meters in length. It grows larger by repeatedly shedding skin.

384.name: Dratini

attacks.name: Wrap
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Paralyzed.

384.flavor: The capture of the first Dratini inspired the search for other legendary Pokemon.

385.name: Dragonair

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads.

attacks.name: Hyper Beam
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon has any Energy cards attached to it, choose 1 of them and discard it.

385.flavor: It is said to live in seas and lakes. Even though it has no wings, it has been seen flying occasionally.

386.name: Dark Dragonair

attacks.name: Evolutionary Light
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may search your deck for an Evolution card. Show it to your opponent and put it into your hand. Shuffle your deck afterward. This power can't be used if Dark Dragonair is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Tail Strike
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 damage plus 20 more damage; if tails, this attack does 20 damage.

386.flavor: As is fitting for a legendary Pokemon, it has many strange powers, including the ability to make rain or snow fall.

387.name: Dragonite

attacks.name: Healing Wind
attacks.text: When you put Dragonite into play, remove 2 damage counters from each of your Pokemon. If a Pokemon has fewer damage counters than that, remove all of them from that Pokemon.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage times the number of heads.

387.flavor: An extremely rarely seen marine Pokemon. Its intelligence is said to match that of humans.

388.name: Dragonite

attacks.name: Special Delivery
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), you may draw a card. If you do, choose a card from your hand and put it on top of your deck. This power can't be used if Dragonite is Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Supersonic Flight
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

388.flavor: This Pokemon can fly in spite of its large bulk. It is said to be able to circumnavigate the earth in just 16 hours.

389.name: Dragonite

attacks.name: Step In
attacks.text: Once during your turn (before your attack), if Dragonite is on your Bench, you may switch it with your Active Pokemon.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 40 damage times the number of heads.

389.flavor: It can fly in spite of its big and bulky physique. It circles the globe in just 16 hours.

390.name: Dark Dragonite

attacks.name: Summon Minions
attacks.text: When you play Dark Dragonite from your hand, search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokemon and put them onto your Bench. Shuffle your deck afterward.

attacks.name: Giant Tail
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

390.flavor: Sometimes called "The God of Destruction." Its wings are able to support it in spite of its massive weight.

391.name: Togepi

attacks.name: Snivel
attacks.text: If the Defending Pokemon attacks Togepi during your opponent's next turn, any damage done to Togepi is reduced by 20 (before applying Weakness and Resistance). (Benching either Pokemon ends this effect.)

attacks.name: Mini-Metronome
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, choose 1 of the Defending Pokemon's attacks. Mini-Metronome copies that attack except for its Energy cost. (You must still do anything else in order to use that attack.) (No matter what type the Defending Pokemon is, Togepi's type is still Colorless.) Togepi performs that attack.

391.flavor: Still only a hatchling, it uses poison to chase off its enemies when threatened.

392.name: Lugia

attacks.name: Aeroblast
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 damage plus 20 more damage for each heads.

392.flavor: It is said that it quietly spends its time deep at the bottom of the sea because its powers are too strong.

393.name: Super Potion
393.text: Discard 1 Energy card attached to 1 of your own Pokemon in order to remove up to 4 damage counters from that Pokemon.

394.name: Imakuni?
394.text: Your Active Pokemon is now Confused. This card cannot be put down on the field as a Pokemon.

395.name: Energy Removal
395.text: Choose 1 Energy card attached to 1 of your opponent's Pokemon and discard it.

396.name: Energy Retrieval
396.text: Trade 1 of the other cards in your hand for up to 2 basic Energy cards from your discard pile.

397.name: Energy Search
397.text: Search your deck for a basic Energy card and put it into your hand. Shuffle your deck afterward.

398.name: Professor Oak
398.text: Discard your hand, then draw 7 cards.

399.name: Fossil Excavation
399.text: You may search your deck for a Mysterious Fossil or choose 1 Mysterious Fossil in your discard pile. Show that card to your opponent and put it into your hand. Either way, shuffle your deck afterward.

400.name: Potion
400.text: Remove up to 2 damage counters from 1 of your Pokemon.

401.name: Gambler
401.text: Shuffle your hand into your deck. Flip a coin. If heads, draw 8 cards. If tails, draw 1 card.

402.name: Revive
402.text: Put 1 Basic Pokemon card from your discard pile onto your Bench. Put damage counters on that Pokemon equal to half its HP (rounded down to the nearest 10). (You can't play Revive if your Bench is full.)

403.name: Max Revive
403.text: Discard 2 Energy cards from your hand in order to put 1 Basic Pokemon from your discard pile onto your Bench. (You can't play Max Revive if your Bench is full.)

404.name: Super Scoop Up
404.text: Flip a coin. If heads, return 1 of your Pokemon and all cards attached to it to your hand.

405.name: Devolution Spray
405.text: Choose 1 of your own Pokemon in play and a Stage of Evolution. Discard all Evolution cards of that Stage or higher attached to that Pokemon. That Pokemon is no longer Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or anything else that might be the result of an attack (just as if you had evolved it).

406.name: Item Finder
406.text: Discard 2 of the other cards from your hand in order to put a Trainer card from your discard pile into your hand.

407.name: Challenge!
407.text: Ask your opponent if he or she accepts your challenge. If your opponent declines (or if both Benches are full), draw 2 cards. If your opponent accepts, each of you searches your decks for any number of Basic Pokemon cards and puts them face down onto your Benches. (A player can't do this if his or her Bench is full.) When you both have finished, shuffle your decks and turn those cards face up.

408.name: Super Energy Retrieval
408.text: Trade 2 of the other cards in your hand for 4 Energy cards from your discard pile. If you have fewer than 4 Energy cards there, take all of them.

409.name: Super Energy Removal
409.text: Discard 1 Energy card attached to 1 of your own Pokemon in order to choose 1 of your opponent's Pokemon and up to 2 Energy cards attached to it. Discard those Energy cards.

410.name: Moon Stone
410.text: You may search your deck for a Colorless Evolution card, show it to your opponent, and put it into your hand. Shuffle your deck afterward.

411.name: Defender
411.text: Attach Defender to 1 of your Pokemon. At the end of your opponent's next turn, discard Defender. Damage done to that Pokemon by attacks is reduced by 20 (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

412.name: Gust of Wind
412.text: Choose 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokemon and switch it with his or her Active Pokemon.

413.name: Mysterious Fossil
413.text: Play Mysterious Fossil as if it were a Basic Pokemon. While in play, Mysterious Fossil counts as a Pokemon (instead of a Trainer card). Mysterious Fossil has no attacks, can't retreat, and can't be Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned. If Mysterious Fossil is Knocked Out, it doesn't count as a Knocked Out Pokemon. (Discard it anyway.) At any time during your turn before your attack, you may discard Mysterious Fossil from play.

414.name: Full Heal
414.text: Your Active Pokemon is no longer Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned.

415.name: Imposter Oak's Revenge
415.text: Discard a card from your hand in order to play this card. Your opponent shuffles his or her hand into his or her deck, then draws 4 cards.

416.name: Impostor Professor Oak
416.text: Your opponent shuffles his or her hand into his or her deck, then draws 7 cards.

417.name: Sleep!
417.text: Flip a coin. If heads, the Defending Pokemon is now Asleep.

419.name: Computer Search
419.text: Discard 2 of the other cards from your hand in order to search your deck for any card and put it into your hand. Shuffle your deck afterward.

420.name: Digger
420.text: Flip a coin. If tails, do 10 damage to your Active Pokemon. If heads, your opponent flips a coin. If tails, your opponent does 10 damage to his or her Active Pokemon. If heads, you flip a coin. Keep doing this until a player gets tails.

421.name: Clefairy Doll
421.text: Play Clefairy Doll as if it were a Basic Pokemon. While in play, Clefairy Doll counts as a Pokemon (instead of a Trainer card). Clefairy Doll has no attacks, can't retreat, and can't be Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed, or Poisoned. If Clefairy Doll is Knocked Out, it doesn't count as a Knocked Out Pokemon. At any time during your turn before your attack, you may discard Clefairy Doll.

422.name: Mr. Fuji
422.text: Choose a Pokemon on your Bench. Shuffle it and any cards attached to it into your deck.

423.name: PlusPower
423.text: Attach PlusPower to your Active Pokemon. At the end of your turn, discard PlusPower. If this Pokemon's attack does damage to the Defending Pokemon (after applying Weakness and Resistance), the attack does 10 more damage to the Defending Pokemon.

425.name: Scoop Up
425.text: Choose 1 of your Pokemon in play and return its Basic Pokemon card to your hand. (Discard all cards attached to that card.)

426.name: Pokemon Trader
426.text: Trade 1 of the Basic Pokemon or Evolution cards in your hand for 1 of the Basic Pokemon or Evolution cards from your deck. Show both cards to your opponent. Shuffle your deck afterward.

427.name: Pokemon Retransfer
427.text: Put an Evolution card from your discard pile on top of your deck.

428.name: Pokedex
428.text: Look at up to 5 cards from the top of your deck and rearrange them as you like.

429.name: Pokemon Center
429.text: Remove all damage counters from all of your own Pokemon with damage counters on them, then discard all Energy cards attached to those Pokemon.

430.name: Pokemon Breeder
430.text: Put a Stage 2 Evolution card from your hand on the matching Basic Pokemon. You can only play this card when you would be allowed to evolve that Pokemon anyway.

431.name: Pokemon Flute
431.text: Choose 1 Basic Pokemon card from your opponent's discard pile and put it onto his or her Bench. (You can't play Pokemon Flute if your opponent's Bench is full.)

432.name: The Boss's Way
432.text: Search your deck for an Evolution card with Dark Pokemon. Show it to your opponent and put it into your hand. Shuffle your deck afterward.

433.name: Goop Gas Attack
433.text: All Pokemon Powers stop working until the end of your opponent's next turn.

435.name: Bill's Teleporter
435.text: Flip a coin. If heads, draw 4 cards.

436.name: Bill's PC
436.text: This card is needed to exchange either an Omanyte, Haunter, Machoke, Graveler, or Kadabra for its corresponding Evolution card.

437.name: Master Ball
437.text: Look at 7 cards from the top of your deck. You may choose a Basic Pokemon or Evolution card from those cards, show it your opponent, then put it into your hand. Shuffle the rest into your deck.

438.name: Lass
438.text: You and your opponent show each other your hands, then shuffle all the Trainer cards from your hands into your decks.

439.name: Maintenance
439.text: Shuffle 2 of the other cards from your hand into your deck in order to draw a card.

441.name: Nightly Garbage Run
441.text: Choose up to 3 Basic Pokemon cards, Evolution cards, and/or basic Energy cards from your discard pile. Show them to your opponent and shuffle them into your deck.

442.name: Recycle
442.text: Flip a coin. If heads, put a card in your discard pile on top of your deck.

443.name: Rocket's Sneak Attack
443.text: Look at your opponent's hand. If he or she has any Trainer cards, choose 1 of them. Your opponent shuffles that card into his or her deck.

444.name: Here Comes Team Rocket!
444.text: Each player plays with his or her Prize cards face up for the rest of the game.

445.name: The Rocket's Trap
445.text: Flip a coin. If heads, choose up to 3 cards at random from your opponent's hand (don't look at them). Your opponent shuffles those cards into his or her deck.
